title: Preparation and Analysis of In Vitro Three Dimensional Breast Carcinoma Surrogates
protocol: Thaw BM component overnight at 4 °C on ice.
Warm medium to 37 °C.
Use Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) plus 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Remove medium from culture dish of near confluent 231 cells and add 1.5 ml Trypsin/EDTA.
Incubate for 1 to 3 min at 37 °C, monitoring for cell detachment.
Stop the reaction by adding 3 ml of medium containing serum once cells start to round and come off the plate.
Pipette the medium and cells into a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the medium and cells at 150 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and re-suspend the cell pellet in 2 ml medium.
Count the number of cells per volume using trypan blue and a hemocytometer.
Repeat the process with other cell types to be included in the surrogate, such as CAF.
Place the appropriate volume of each cell suspension into a 15 ml conical tube (one tube for each cell type).
Centrifuge the medium and cells at 150 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Re-suspend one cell type in cell culture grade water (178.8 μl).
Re-suspend the other cell type in 10x DMEM (100 μl containing phenol red to monitor pH).
Place the tubes containing the cells on ice and proceed quickly to preparation of ECM below.
Limit the time that the cells remain in water to preserve viability.
On ice, add components listed into a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube in order.
Add cell culture grade water containing the desired number of 231 cells (determined above).
Add collagen I (10 mg/ml bovine), drop by drop.
Add basement membrane, thawed.
Add 10x DMEM (containing phenol red) with the desired number of CAF (determined above).
Add 7.5% sodium bicarbonate, drop by drop.
Gently mix by pipetting, avoiding formation of bubbles.
Monitor pH level using phenol red in the 10x DMEM.
Check that mixture is an orange/pink color indicating a pH of ~7.
If pH is too low (too yellow), slowly add additional 7.5% sodium bicarbonate one drop at a time until appropriate color is reached.
Keep mixture on ice and work quickly to prevent premature ECM polymerization.
Label the lid of a sterile 8-well chamber slide to indicate experimental variations.
Keep the chamber slide on ice.
Pipette 100 µl of the cell+ECM mixture into each well, starting from the edges for better distribution.
Incubate surrogates at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 45 min to allow ECM polymerization.
Add 100 µl culture media to each well after ECM polymerization.
Incubate with added culture media at 37 °C and 5% CO2, changing the medium every two days.
Sterilize all bioreactor components using autoclaving for 12 min at 121.1 °C followed by drying for 15 min.
Incubate components in 70% ethanol for 1 hr.
Prepare and assemble the portion of the bioreactor system that will house the surrogate.
Insert a PDMS foam backbone into the PDMS flow channel tubing using forceps.
Push four polymer-coated stainless steel wires into the PDMS foam to generate parallel microchannels.
Inject the cell+ECM mixture into the bioreactor component housing the surrogates using a 26 gauge needle with syringe.
Place the bioreactor component containing cells into a 50 ml conical tube and continuously rotate at ~18 rpm while incubating at 37 °C for 45 min to allow ECM polymerization.
Remove the stainless steel wires prior to connecting the bioreactor assembly to the perfusion pump.
Start medium perfusion in an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2 with a bulk flow rate of 167.1 µl/min and microchannel wall shear stress of 1 dyne/cm².
Label cryomolds and plastic tissue cassettes for surrogate fixation and processing.
Melt specimen processing gel in a 60 °C water bath until liquefied.
Pipette approximately 300 μl of melted specimen processing gel into the bottom of each labeled cryomold.
Carefully remove the surrogate from the bioreactor or well of an 8-well chamber slide using a scalpel blade and forceps.
Place the surrogate into the cryomold containing specimen processing gel.
Pipette approximately 300 µl specimen processing gel to cover the surrogate in the cryomold.
Incubate at 4 °C for 30 min to solidify.
Remove the specimen processing gel containing the surrogate from the cryomold and place it into a tissue cassette.
Place the tissue cassette containing the surrogate into 10% neutral buffered formalin for 10 to 12 hr at room temperature to allow complete fixation.
Move the tissue cassette containing the surrogate to 70% ethanol until processed to paraffin.
Section the surrogates using a standard microtome for sectioning of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues.
Place histologic sections on plain glass slides.
Bake the histologic sections at 58 °C for 10-12 hours to prepare for staining.
Immerse the sections in xylene for 5 minutes.
Repeat immersion of sections in xylene for 5 minutes.
Repeat immersion of sections in xylene for 5 minutes.
Wash sections with 100% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing of sections with 100% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Immerse the sections in 95% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Repeat immersion of sections in 95% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Rinse the sections with tap water for 5 minutes.
Wash sections with de-ionized water for 5 minutes.
Stain sections with hematoxylin for 5 minutes.
Rinse the sections with tap water for 5 minutes.
Clarify staining by dipping in clarifier solution.
Rinse the sections with tap water for 5 minutes.
Treat sections with bluing reagent for 30 seconds.
Wash sections with tap water for 5 minutes.
Immerse the sections in 95% ethanol and dip ten times.
Stain sections with eosin-Y for 1 minute.
Immerse the sections in 95% ethanol and dip ten times.
Mount a coverslip to each slide using mounting media.
Allow mounting media to dry before imaging.
Image at least one entire H&E stained histologic section of the surrogate using brightfield microscopy at 400X magnification, saving the images as .tif files.
Open an image (.tif file) of the surrogate in ImageJ.
Select "Set Measurements" (under the "Analyze" tab) and select "Area".
Outline the area of the surrogate in the image by dragging the mouse and clicking to make anchor points using the polygon tool.
Select "Measure" under the "Analyze" tab.
Repeat for each image of the tissue surrogate.
Save measurements and corresponding image identifiers to a spreadsheet program.
Upload image files used to measure area into CellProfiler by dragging them to the "File List".
Assign a name to the images imported in the "NamesAndTypes" input module.
Select the image type (i.e., "Color Image").
Create an analysis pipeline that includes the following modules to calculate the number of cells per image.
Click the "+" sign next to "Adjust Module".
Select "ColorToGray".
Select the input image name from the drop down menu.
Name the output image.
Select the original image type (i.e., RGB if color image input).
Select "ImageMath".
Select the "Invert" operation.
Name the output image.
Select the grayscale image in the "select first image" tab.
Select "IdentifyPrimaryObjects".
Select input image after math correction.
Name the primary object to be identified as nuclei.
Enter the diameter range for nuclei in pixel units, approximately 25 to 65.
Select "adaptive" threshold strategy with "Otsu" thresholding method and "three classes".
Identify secondary objects using the input image (image after math correction) and nuclei.
Name the objects to be identified as cells.
Choose the "propagation" method for identifying secondary objects.
Use the "adaptive" threshold strategy and "Otsu" method with "two classes", minimizing "weighted variance".
Select "no smoothing" and a threshold correction factor of 1.
Set lower and upper bounds of 0 and 1, respectively.
Specify a regularization factor of 0.05.
Measure object size and shape for cells (secondary object) and nuclei (primary object).
Name the output objects.
Filter the nuclei (primary object).
Keep the next two parameters as per the default settings.
Select "AreaShape" as the measurement to filter by category.
Select "FormFactor" as the measurement.
Select "Yes" to filter using a minimum measurement value and add a minimum value of 0.52.
Select "No" to filter using a maximum measurement.
Select "Yes" to retain the outlines of filtered objects and name the outlined image.
Select "ExportToSpreadsheet".
Start "Test Mode" in CellProfiler and evaluate each step, including that the nuclei in the test image are appropriately filtered.
Ensure optimal parameters were chosen to identify cells.
Save the project.
Click "Analyze Images".
Open the spreadsheet containing image data generated by CellProfiler.
Copy the filtered nuclei data from column D in the CellProfiler spreadsheet.
Copy the image identifiers from column R in the CellProfiler spreadsheet.
Paste the copied nuclei data and image identifiers into the spreadsheet with measured area data.
Calculate the sum of all measurements for the number of nuclei per image.
Calculate the sum of measurements for surrogate area from each image.
Divide the total area measurement by 1x10^6.
Divide the total number of nuclei by the result obtained in the previous step to get cells per 1x10^6 pixels^2.
